implementation_notes: The modern .NET realization groups broker operations: ServiceBusClient.CreateTransactionAsync() returns a ServiceBusTransactionContext that is passed to SendMessageAsync/CompleteMessageAsync and closed by CommitTransactionAsync() or RollbackTransactionAsync(), so a receive-complete-send group is atomic on the broker. It covers Service Bus operations only; making a database write part of the same commit is not possible through this scope, so database-coupled services write an outbox row in the EF Core transaction instead and let a relay publish it, or fall back to the ambient TransactionScope path.
pitfalls: A Service Bus transaction groups broker operations only: wrapping it around a DbContext.SaveChanges call does not make the database write atomic with the send.
Transactions cannot span namespaces, and settling messages from different entities requires them to live in one namespace; otherwise the commit throws.
The transaction must be committed or rolled back on every path - an exception between send and commit leaves the broker to time it out.

variants.name: Ambient TransactionScope with a transactional MSMQ queue and an enlisted database
variants.implementation_notes: The classic .NET realization is the only in-language path where the database and the queue share one commit: new TransactionScope() opens an ambient transaction, System.Messaging.MessageQueue.Send with MessageQueueTransactionType.Automatic enlists the transactional queue, SqlConnection.EnlistTransaction(Transaction.Current) enlists the database, and scope.Complete() commits both through the distributed transaction coordinator. Its price is a Windows-only stack (transactional queues, MSMQ and the DTC), automatic promotion to a distributed transaction as soon as the second resource joins, and a legacy API set.
pitfalls: MSMQ, transactional queues and the DTC are Windows-only and increasingly legacy, so treat this as an inheritance path rather than a green-field choice.
Ambient transactions promote to a distributed transaction as soon as a second resource joins, and promotion failures surface as opaque TransactionAbortedException.
TransactionScope is thread-static: with async/await you must pass TransactionScopeAsyncFlowOption.Enabled or the ambient transaction is lost after the first await.
